## chapter_1_introduction

- [Tutorial 0: Visualization](scripts/chapter_1_introduction/tutorial_0_visualization.py): Plot a simulated image with **PyAutoGalaxy**, compare views of the dataset, and adjust the display so you can inspect its structure. This tutorial introduces the plotting tools used throughout the course.

- [HowToGalaxy: Introduction](scripts/chapter_1_introduction/tutorial_1_grids_and_galaxies.py): Galaxies have a wide range of appearances: some are smooth and rounded, while others have discs, spiral arms or irregular structure. These visible features make up a galaxy’s **morphology**.
  - Contents: Grids, Geometry, Light Profiles, One Dimension Projection, Galaxies, Unit Conversion, Wrap Up, Advanced Topics, Other Unit Conversion, Over Sampling
- [Tutorial 2: Data](scripts/chapter_1_introduction/tutorial_2_data.py): In the previous tutorial, we used light profiles to create images of galaxies. However, those images don't accurately represent what we would observe through a telescope.
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Optics Blurring, Poisson Noise, Background Sky, Simulator, Output, Interferometer Data, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 3: Fitting](scripts/chapter_1_introduction/tutorial_3_fitting.py): In previous tutorials, we used light profiles to create simulated images of galaxies and visualized how these images would appear when captured by a CCD detector on a telescope like the Hubble Space Telescope.
  - Contents: Dataset, Mask, Masked Grid, Fitting, Incorrect Fit, Model Fitting, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 4: Methods](scripts/chapter_1_introduction/tutorial_4_methods.py): This tutorial is not written yet, but will explain in more detail the different methods used to fit and analyse galaxies.

  - Contents: Initial Setup, Object Composition, Visualization, Code Design, Source Code, Wrap Up

## chapter_2_modeling

- [Tutorial 1: Non-linear Search](scripts/chapter_2_modeling/tutorial_1_non_linear_search.py): In chapter 1, you adjusted a galaxy model by hand and inspected how well its image matched the data. Now we will ask a search to do this for us. Our aim is still to learn about the galaxy: its size, shape and concentration.
  - Contents: Parameter Space, Dataset and Mask, Model and Priors, Analysis, Nested Sampling, Result
- [Tutorial 2: Practicalities](scripts/chapter_2_modeling/tutorial_2_practicalities.py): A galaxy can contain a compact bulge and an extended disk. We now fit both, while learning how to run a search, manage its memory use and inspect its output. These practical skills let us assess a model as the fit progresses.
  - Contents: Dataset and Mask, Model, Search Settings, Analysis and Run Times, VRAM Use, Output Folder, Unique Identifier, Results and Configuration
- [Tutorial 3: Why Modeling Is Hard](scripts/chapter_2_modeling/tutorial_3_why_modeling_is_hard.py): The bulge and disk in tutorial 2 made our model more realistic, but also harder to fit. Their centres, shapes, brightnesses and sizes can trade off. A search can find a plausible galaxy without finding the best explanation available within the model.
  - Contents: A Reference Fit, An Inadequate Search, Local Maxima, Prior Tuning, Reducing Complexity, Look Harder, Benefits and Weaknesses
- [Tutorial 4: Linear Profiles](scripts/chapter_2_modeling/tutorial_4_linear_profiles.py): In tutorial 3, simplifying the bulge and disk geometry made the search easier but restricted the galaxies it could represent. Linear light profiles offer a different opportunity: keep the same profile shapes and solve their intensities directly, removing those dimensions from the non-linear search.
  - Contents: Linear Light Profiles, Results and Intensities, Galaxy Structure, Basis, Two Gaussian Groups, Benefits and Limitations
- [Tutorial 5: Data and Likelihoods](scripts/chapter_2_modeling/tutorial_5_data_and_likelihoods.py): So far we have changed the galaxy model and the search. Now consider the other side of the fit: the measurements we include and how they are compared with a prediction. The data, model and Analysis object have distinct jobs. This separation lets the same modelling tools work with different observations and likelihood functions.
  - Contents: Masking, Extra Galaxy Noise Scaling, Analysis, Interferometer Data, Multiple Datasets
- [Tutorial 6: Search Chaining](scripts/chapter_2_modeling/tutorial_6_search_chaining.py): A neighbouring galaxy can complicate the fit to our target. We need to describe its light, but repeatedly searching all its parameters while refining the target can waste effort and introduce difficult degeneracies. Search chaining lets us fit different parts of the scene in stages.
  - Contents: Dataset, Search 1, Inspect Before Chaining, Search 2, Limits and Pipelines
- [Tutorial 7: Summary](scripts/chapter_2_modeling/tutorial_7_summary.py): (no summary in script docstring)

## chapter_3_pixelizations

- [Tutorial 1: Pixelizations](scripts/chapter_3_pixelizations/tutorial_1_pixelizations.py): In the previous chapters, we used light profiles to model the light of a galaxy, where the light profile was an analytic description of how the luminosity varies as a function of radius.
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Mesh, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 2: Mappers](scripts/chapter_3_pixelizations/tutorial_2_mappers.py): In the previous tutorial, we used a pixelization to create a `Mapper`. However, it was not clear what a `Mapper` does, why it was called a mapper and whether it was mapping anything at all!
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Mappers, Mask, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 3: Inversions](scripts/chapter_3_pixelizations/tutorial_3_inversions.py): In the previous two tutorials, we introduced:
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Pixelization, Positive Only Solver, Detailed Explanation, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 4: Bayesian Regularization](scripts/chapter_3_pixelizations/tutorial_4_bayesian_regularization.py): So far, we have:
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Convenience Function, Pixelization, Regularization, Bayesian Evidence, Non-Linear and Linear, Detailed Description, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 5: Bayesian Formalism](scripts/chapter_3_pixelizations/tutorial_5_bayesian_formalism.py): In tutorials 1 to 4, we built an intuition for how pixelized galaxy reconstruction works: pixelizations place a pixel-grid over the galaxy's image, mappers pair pixelization pixels with image-pixels, inversions solve for the pixel fluxes that best fit the data, and regularization smooths the solution within a Bayesian framework.
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Mask, Over Sampling, Mesh Shape, Galaxy, Image Grid, Mesh Pixel Centres, Interpolation, Mapper, Mapping Matrix, Blurred Mapping Matrix, Data Vector (D), Curvature Matrix (F), Unregularized Solve, Regularization Matrix (H), Galaxy Reconstruction (s), Image Reconstruction, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Regularization Term, Complexity Terms, Noise Normalization Term, Log Evidence, Fit, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 6: Model Fit](scripts/chapter_3_pixelizations/tutorial_6_model_fit.py): In the previous tutorials we used an inversion to reconstruct a complex galaxy. However, from the perspective of a scientific analysis, it is not clear how useful this was. When we fit a galaxy with light profiles, we learn about its brightness (`intensity`), size (`effective_radius`), compactness (`sersic_index`), etc.
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Model + Search + Analysis + Model-Fit (Search 1), Mesh Shape, Model + Search + Analysis + Model-Fit (Search 2), Model + Search (Search 3), Wrap Up

## chapter_4_scaling_up_galaxies

- [Tutorial 1: Extra Galaxies](scripts/chapter_4_scaling_up_galaxies/tutorial_1_extra_galaxies.py): Welcome to chapter 4 of **HowToGalaxy**, where we scale up galaxy modeling beyond a single galaxy.
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Dataset Auto-Simulation, The Decision, Mask, Approach 1 Noise Scaling, Noise Scaling Fit, Approach 2 Extra Galaxies Model, Extra Galaxy Centres, Extra Galaxies Model Composition, Extra Galaxies Fit, Which Approach When, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 2: Multi-Galaxy Blends](scripts/chapter_4_scaling_up_galaxies/tutorial_2_multi_galaxy.py): In the previous tutorial, we learned how to deal with extra galaxies near the galaxy we care about — nuisance objects whose light contaminates the data but which are not themselves the subject of our study. We removed their emission from the analysis, or gave them a heavily restricted model, and the single galaxy we were studying remained the star of the show.
  - Contents: Initial Setup, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Mask, Over Sampling, Why Not Fit Them Separately?, Model, Fixing the Centres, Model Fit, Result, Light Decomposition Degeneracy, Wrap Up
- [Tutorial 3: Cluster](scripts/chapter_4_scaling_up_galaxies/tutorial_3_cluster.py): Throughout this chapter we have been scaling up: from a single galaxy with extra galaxies nearby, to blended multi-galaxy systems where every galaxy received its own free light model.
  - Contents: The Scaling Problem, Dataset, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Member Catalogue, Masking, Model, Search + Analysis, Model Fit, Result, Per-Member Results, Refinements, Wrap Up

## chapter_optional

- [Optional Tutorial: Need for Speed](scripts/chapter_optional/tutorial_need_for_speed.py): Return to this tutorial when a fit is too slow for your scientific needs. Faster likelihood calculations help, but a well-organised model and search often matter just as much. Hardware cannot make an inappropriate model fit.
  - Contents: Search Effort, Likelihood Cost, JAX and Batching, Measuring Runtime, Data Quantity
- [Optional Historical Tutorial: Prior Passing](scripts/chapter_optional/tutorial_prior_passing.py): This is historical background, not part of the recommended HowToGalaxy learning path. Older versions of the PyAutoGalaxy / PyAutoLens workflow automatically narrowed priors between searches. That default behaviour has been disabled. New readers are discouraged from investing time in the old prior-passing recipes: learn the component-separation approach in chapter 2 tutorial 6 instead.
  - Contents: Historical Behaviour, Current Behaviour, Why It Is Optional
- [Optional Tutorial: Alternative Searches](scripts/chapter_optional/tutorial_searches.py): You can complete HowToGalaxy using Nautilus without studying search algorithms in detail. Return here if you want to understand the fast Prodigy stage of search chaining, or compare alternative approaches for your own work.
  - Contents: Optimisation, Nested Sampling, MCMC

## simulators

It is used in chapter 4 of the **HowToGalaxy** lectures, where the member population is modeled via a **catalogue**: a CSV of member centres and luminosities whose photometry pins the faint galaxies while only a shared normalization stays free.
